quizzes.stem: A company runs forty applications, and most of them call a model that is still active. The deprecation table shows its retirement date nine weeks away, marked tentative. What should the platform team do?

options.a: Start testing the replacement now, so that the roll-out can end well ahead of the cut-off
options.b: Hold the work until the date is confirmed final, so no effort goes on a date that may shift
options.c: Switch every application to the replacement this week, since the date may still come sooner
options.d: Plan to keep the model in use past that date, since a tentative date is not one that is enforced

explanation.a: The advice is to "consider thorough testing of your applications with the new models well before the retirement date", and "Sixty days is the shortest warning, and a migration of forty applications can take longer than that", so testing starts now and the plan ends well ahead of the date.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a tentative date on an active model "is never a date to wait for".
explanation.c: Ruled out because such a date "marks a date that may move later", not sooner, and the replacement is "where to begin testing, and the decision is yours to make on your own tasks".
explanation.d: Ruled out because once the date arrives "Requests to retired models will fail".

quizzes.stem: A model that several of a team's applications call is listed as legacy, with no retirement scheduled for it yet. The team asks whether its migration plan can wait. What should they decide?

options.a: Switch to the named replacement today, since a legacy listing comes with a successor and a date
options.b: Let the plan wait for a retirement date, since the 60-day notice leaves time to move then
options.c: Begin the move early, since updates have stopped and any later cut-off comes with finite notice
options.d: Reroute every call at once, since legacy is the state in which requests to the model fail

explanation.c: Legacy means "The model will no longer receive updates and may be deprecated in the future", and once a date is set "There is notice, and it is finite", so the plan starts before any retirement date exists.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the successor and the date belong to the deprecated state, where "Anthropic provides a recommended replacement and assigns a retirement date".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Sixty days is the shortest warning, and a migration of forty applications can take longer than that".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Requests to retired models will fail" describes the retired state, not legacy.

quizzes.stem: In this module's example, a staged roll-out sits at 5 percent of traffic, with a minimum of 1,000 requests per stage and a limit of 5 errors per thousand. The stage has served 300 requests with no errors. What is the next step?

options.a: Advance to 25 percent, since a stage that shows no errors at all has proved itself healthy
options.b: Hold the share and keep counting, since it has too little evidence yet to be judged either way
options.c: Roll back to zero, since a stage short of its request count is treated as a failure
options.d: Move all traffic to the new model, since the gate already passed on the regression suite

explanation.b: 300 is below the example's minimum of 1,000, and a stage with fewer requests than the minimum says nothing yet, so the rule is to hold at the stage.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A stage with fewer requests than the minimum (1,000 in the example) says nothing yet".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the share goes back to zero only when errors pass the limit: "Over it, the share goes back to zero".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Passing a suite is a prediction about traffic, and traffic is where it is tested".

quizzes.stem: A staged roll-out at 25 percent of requests has served 50,000 requests with 400 errors, and the limit is 5 errors per thousand. What happens next?

options.a: Drop to 5 percent and keep the roll-out running, to gather more evidence from a smaller share
options.b: Hold at 25 percent and investigate the errors before choosing which way to move
options.c: Advance to 100 percent so that the failure shows up clearly in the data of the whole base
options.d: Set the share back to zero so that all traffic goes to the previous model again

explanation.d: 400 errors in 50,000 requests is 8 per thousand, over the limit, so the share goes back to zero and the previous model, still configured, takes the traffic.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Holding at the stage while errors continue leaves the share of customers who see them where it is".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Advancing to 100 percent to see the failure in the full data makes every customer the sample".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Reducing to a smaller share keeps part of the damage on the path".

quizzes.stem: The new model costs about a third more per answer and fixes the refund errors. The product owner asks whether to move. What should the architect reply?

options.a: Show both figures and advise staying, because a third more per answer outweighs the refund fix
options.b: Show both figures and advise moving, because the vendor named the newer model as the replacement
options.c: Show both figures and let them decide, because staying put also ends on a fixed retirement date
options.d: Show both figures and defer the choice, because more evidence on cost arrives as retirement nears

explanation.c: The architect's job "is to state the trade", including "the date that forces the choice", and the owner decides, since "staying has a date that ends it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A recommended replacement is a starting point, not a decision".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A rise in cost is a number to put before the owner, not a verdict".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Waiting for the retirement date hands the decision to the calendar, and gives up the rollback".

quizzes.stem: After a migration, a parser that reads `content[0].text` breaks on some replies and works on others. Which step was missed?

options.a: Lowering max_tokens so that the thinking is cut off before the text of the reply begins
options.b: Picking out the blocks to use by the kind that each one declares, on every answer received
options.c: Turning thinking off by sending the disabled setting, which the new model accepts as before
options.d: Dropping the first block of every reply before parsing, since it always holds only thinking

explanation.b: With adaptive thinking on by default "the first content block of a reply may be thinking text", so the parser must "Read content blocks by `type`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "`max_tokens` covers thinking plus text, and thinking tokens are billed as output tokens", so a lower limit cuts the text as well.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the guide lists `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` among the "five settings that return a 400 error".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A reply need not begin with thinking text either, so a rule that always drops the first block loses real text".

quizzes.stem: On the day the new model took all traffic, the team deleted the old model's id from its configuration to keep it tidy. Two days later errors spike. What did the cleanup take away?

options.a: Nothing, since faults that surface after a passed gate are fixed forward on the new model
options.b: The cost baseline, since a new baseline is set by billing the old model beside the new one
options.c: The latency check, whose p95 limit the gate reads from the old model's live timings
options.d: The way back, since no tested fallback remains to receive requests while the fault is fixed

explanation.d: The page says "the old model is the rollback, and it stays so until its own retirement date".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "When the limit is passed, the response is to send every request back to the previous model", not to fix forward.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a new baseline comes from the new model's own traffic: "measure usage afresh, set a new baseline".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the gate's latency check takes "the nearest-rank 95th percentile of the new timings, against a limit".
